blocking.issue: The new process joins every SO_REUSEPORT group before it is ready or accepted. Once a TCP socket listens, or a UDP socket binds, the kernel hashes new connections to it. That breaks readiness gating (ADR-0015) and ZG-3 in three ways. First, some 9901 probes reach the new process while it is still warming, and its /readyz returns 503 until warm-up ends. Second, client connections queue on a process that has not been accepted, and if the handover is refused or times out (60 s), the new process exits and its queued connections are reset. Third, half of the in-flight QUIC flows on UDP 8443 break at bind time, even if the handover is later refused. Steering happens only in step 5, which is too late.
blocking.evidence: Line 174: "3. **Bind and gate.** It binds 8080, 8443 and 9901 with `SO_REUSEPORT` (in-flight QUIC on UDP 8443 is lost), warms, then reports version, format markers and active digest over the owner-only Unix socket"; line 175: "A new process not accepted within 60 s (target) exits; the old one never started draining."; line 53: "ZG-3 | An in-place handover refuses no new TCP connection and keeps the Node's `/readyz` at 200 throughout"
blocking.fix: Specify pinning. The lock holder attaches, at startup and after every listener bind, an `SO_ATTACH_REUSEPORT_CBPF` program to each of its reuseport groups (8080, 8443 TCP and UDP, 9901) that returns its own socket index, so a new binder gets no connection or datagram until step 5 replaces the program with one that returns the new socket's index. Alternatively, the new process creates TCP sockets with `x/sys/unix` socket and bind and calls listen only after acceptance, but UDP still needs the pin. Update Figure 1 and steps 3 to 5 to match. State that QUIC flows are lost at steering, not at bind. Add a refused-handover case and a 9901 probe check to V-3.

blocking.section: Binary upgrades > In-place handover; Drain timeline defaults
blocking.issue: In a handover, the old process fails /readyz as soon as it starts draining. CBPF steers only new connections, so a balancer that reuses its health-check connection (a keep-alive HTTP checker) keeps probing the old process, gets 503 and marks the Node down. That violates ZG-3 and the V-3 pass criterion of 200 throughout a handover.
blocking.evidence: Figure 1: "Old->>Old: accept the queued connections, close listeners, fail readyz"; Drain table line 190: "0 s | Readiness failure: `/readyz` returns 503; heartbeats set `draining`"; line 389: "200 throughout a handover"
blocking.fix: Define the handover variant of the readiness step. After steering, the old process first closes its idle 9901 connections, then answers any in-flight admin request with `Connection: close`, and only then reports draining. Its /readyz is never served as 503 on a connection it keeps open, since the accepted new process holds readiness for the Node. Add a keep-alive health checker to V-3.

blocking.issue: ZG-1 contradicts the document's own Atomic swap text and Data plane. Streams pinned to a snapshot K + 1 activations old are closed at once, with no grace. Only non-stream requests that are still pinned get the 30 s grace before they end with RZ-RT-014.
blocking.evidence: Line 51: "ZG-1 | A Hot Reload drops no in-flight request; only a stream that outlives K + 1 further activations and a 30 s grace ends, K = 2 (target)". Data plane, Why no in-flight request is dropped: "When a third would be retired, the oldest becomes closing: its streams end at once (WebSocket close 1001, gRPC trailers ... UNAVAILABLE, an SSE end event with a retry hint). After a grace period of 30 s (target) it becomes ending, and anything still pinned ends with `RZ-RT-014`"
blocking.fix: Reword ZG-1: "A Hot Reload drops no in-flight request. A stream pinned to a snapshot K + 1 activations old receives a going-away close at once, and a request still pinned 30 s later (target) ends with RZ-RT-014, K = 2 (target)." Also note Data plane rule 6: during a burst, activation waits for the closing snapshot to be freed.

Under the Release skew table, a Node newer than the Control Store version is outside policy, and Release Figure 2 requires every Node at N-1 before the first replica is replaced. The runbook's generic Before row repeats the error.

blocking.fix: In Prepare, require every Node at N-1 and upgrade any N-2 Node first. Split the runbook Before row into two rows: before a Ruralz Control upgrade (every Node at N-1) and before a Node upgrade after finalize (every Node at N-1 or N).

blocking.issue: After finalize, Figure 4 sends the operator straight to restore. It omits rule 6 of Ruralz Control upgrades, which Release assigns to this document: while still on N, roll out a Revision without N-only fields to every Cluster until `complete`, then return every Node to N-1 by handover, and only then restore (re-applying N-1's `ruralz-crds.yaml`). Following Figure 4 while Nodes run N leaves them newer than the restored Control Store version, which is outside the skew policy.
blocking.evidence: Figure 4: `q5 -- "yes" --> r7` with r7 "Restore: High availability and disaster recovery"; line 377: "After finalize, returning to N-1 is a restore into an empty N-1 deployment ... a recovery, not a rollback". Release rule 6: "If Nodes have already moved to N, rollback after finalize follows a fixed order ... [Zero-downtime upgrades and hot reload] owns the Rollout and handover steps"
blocking.fix: Add a Figure 4 branch, "Nodes already on N?", that leads to "Roll out a Revision without N-only fields to every Cluster, then hand over every Node to N-1" before r7. In the prose, write out the rule 6 Rollout and handover steps that this document owns, with the CRD re-apply order, and link HA/DR for the restore itself.

blocking.issue: ZG-8 promises that every rollback this document owns takes three steps or fewer. Past the binary rollback limit, however, a binary rollback chains a Revision revert (start, a possible RZ-CP-006 approval, status) with a binary rollback (two steps), which makes up to five steps. The revert target is older than the replaced Revision, so RZ-CP-006 approval is likely.
blocking.evidence: Line 58: "ZG-8 | Every rollback this document owns takes three steps or fewer"; line 377: "Past the binary rollback limit, first roll back to a Revision without N-only fields, then the binary."; Figure 4: `r5 --> r4`
blocking.fix: Either add a single table row, "Binary past the rollback limit", with at most three steps (for example, 1: `ruralz rollout start --cluster <c> --revision sha256:<pre-adoption>` plus approval, 2: `ruralz rollout status <id> --wait` reaches `complete`, 3: handover or image back to N-1), or narrow ZG-8 to exclude this path and name the path as a two-stage procedure with its own drill (V-6).

blocking.section: Binary upgrades > In-place handover (step 6, Move identity)
blocking.issue: The new process presents the same certificate and `node.id` as the old one. Control Stream state lives in memory on each replica, so a `Hello` that reaches a different replica before that replica learns the old stream closed can be rejected with RZ-CP-002 ("`node.id` taken"). The document does not define what the new process does then. Treated as fatal, the Node stays detached, and Rollouts quarantine it as lagging.
blocking.evidence: Line 177: "At Drain start the old process sends a last `Heartbeat` with `draining`, closes its Control Stream and releases the lock. The new process takes the lock and dials 8091 with `Hello`". Control plane and GitOps registry: "RZ-CP-002 | `node.id` taken, or `Hello` mismatches the certificate"; Hello row: "`RZ-CP-002`, `RZ-CP-003`, or anchor updates"
blocking.fix: State that during a handover the new process retries RZ-CP-002 with full-jitter backoff (base 1 s, cap 60 s (target)) while it stays ready. Propose that Ruralz Control let a `Hello` from the same certificate supersede a stream whose last `Heartbeat` carried `draining`, and record that as a new OQ owned by control-plane-and-gitops.

blocking.issue: The overlap sizing covers only a second base RSS plus Plugin pools. Every Node ceiling in Data plane is enforced per process: 20,000 connections, 20,000 in-flight units, `maxBufferedBytes`, `maxPluginMemoryBytes` (instances reserve their full limit) and (K + 2) snapshots. During the overlap the old process still holds its long-lived connections and buffers while the new process fills its own ceilings, so the Node's worst case roughly doubles. Data plane sizes that worst case at about 19 GiB plus snapshots on a 32 GiB Node, and nothing bounds the combined total.
blocking.evidence: Line 182: "handover hosts SHOULD keep free memory for a second base RSS, 100 MB plus 2 KB per Route (target), plus its Plugin pools (OQ-zero-downtime-upgrades-and-hot-reload-6)". Data plane, Bounded resources: "Worst-case Node memory sums connections at 592 KiB (about 11.3 GiB), in-flight units ... about 19 GiB plus snapshots, fitting a 32 GiB Node (hypothesis)"
blocking.fix: Make the Node-wide ceilings shared across the overlap. The old process reports its live connection, in-flight unit, buffered-byte and Plugin-memory usage in the Unix-socket exchange, and the new process starts at the ceiling minus that usage, rising as the old process drains. If that is rejected, state the 2x worst case with (hypothesis) and add ceiling sharing as an option to OQ-zero-downtime-upgrades-and-hot-reload-6.

blocking.issue: The replacement path contradicts Deployment topologies. That document sets the Node StatefulSet's `RollingUpdate` `maxUnavailable` to match the PodDisruptionBudget, which is one zone's share at minimum scale, not one Pod. PodDisruptionBudgets limit evictions, not the StatefulSet controller's own rolling update, so "within the PodDisruptionBudget" does not bound the update.
blocking.evidence: Line 132: "Replacement | Kubernetes (T4) | StatefulSet rolling update: preStop, Drain, new Pod | One Pod at a time, within the PodDisruptionBudget"; line 251: "Each step removes one Pod for about 40 to 45 s (hypothesis)". Deployment topologies T4: "Node StatefulSet | `podManagementPolicy: Parallel` ...; `RollingUpdate`, `maxUnavailable` matching the PodDisruptionBudget"; "PodDisruptionBudgets | ... for Nodes, one zone's share at minimum scale (target)"
blocking.fix: Align with Deployment topologies. State that each step replaces up to `maxUnavailable` Pods (one zone's share at minimum scale), recompute the per-step capacity loss and the reconnect load against the 2,000 reconnects per second per Node figure, and bound the update by `maxUnavailable`, not by the PodDisruptionBudget. If one Pod at a time is intended, raise an OQ against deployment-topologies.

non_blocking.suggestion: The two-phase GOAWAY (last stream ID 2^31-1, then a final GOAWAY after a PING round trip) cannot be built on `net/http`'s HTTP/2 server. `Server.Shutdown` sends one GOAWAY with the highest processed stream ID and exposes no server-side frame API, and x/net's `Server` is deprecated (pack 7, ADR-0009). Mark those two table rows as depending on OQ-zero-downtime-upgrades-and-hot-reload-3, and state that the default for Planned (M1) is option (a), a single GOAWAY, whose race clients survive by retrying unprocessed streams.

When a Revision changes a listener on the same port (protocol, TLS, `http3`), rebinding puts two sockets of one process in one reuseport group, and closing the old one drops its queued connections, the same gap HAProxy measured. Prefer keeping the socket and swapping only the handler and TLS config in the snapshot, or apply the in-process CBPF steering the handover uses.

State Data plane rule 6: while a snapshot is closing or ending, the latest pending Revision waits up to the 30 s grace plus the ending bound and compile time (target). PB-7's 500 ms then applies only without a closing snapshot, and Rollout ACK timing (60 s) should be checked against that delay.

Cover two edge cases. (1) The holder's candidate write failed (the full-disk case in Partial failure), so its candidate does not match its active digest: the old process should refuse at once with a reason instead of letting the new process loop until the 60 s timeout. (2) The holder exits during the overlap before acceptance: say whether the new process takes the lock and serves under boot order (1) or exits.

The research file notes that the Kubernetes version in which the preStop `sleep` handler became GA was not verified (scalability-patterns.md, Gaps). Name the minimum supported Kubernetes version, or give an exec fallback, before relying on "needs no binary in the image".
Use one name for 25 s (drain deadline) and 30 s (exit bound). The text says "preStop wait plus the Drain deadline: 45 s against 5 s plus 30 s" while the table puts the Drain deadline at 25 s.

foundation_amendments: Pack section 7, Upgrades row (ADR-0015): add that the lock holder pins its reuseport groups with an SO_ATTACH_REUSEPORT_CBPF program returning its own socket index until it accepts a handover. Without it, SO_REUSEPORT sends connections, UDP datagrams and /readyz probes to a new process before readiness gating.
